**Image Analysis:**

- **Affected part**: Banana leaf (large, broad leaf with visible midrib/vein running diagonally)
- **Color**: Dominant yellow/golden coloration across most of the leaf surface, with patches of remaining green (lower-left area)
- **Pattern/Texture**: Extensive yellowing with scattered dark/black spots and lesions distributed throughout the yellowed tissue
- **Extent**: Widespread — most of the leaf is affected

**Reasoning through the classes:**

- **Anthracnose**: Causes dark, sunken lesions typically on fruit tips — not a good match
- **Bunchy_Top**: Viral; causes stunted, bunched growth architecture with dark-green streaks on midrib/petiole — not this pattern
- **Cigar_End_Rot**: Affects banana fruit tips, not leaves — ruled out
- **Cordana_Leaf_Spot**: Produces discrete oval spots with brown centers and yellow halos — more defined lesions than seen here
- **Panama_Disease**: Fusarium wilt; causes systemic yellowing from outer leaves inward, with internal vascular browning — could partially match, but lacks the characteristic dark lesion overlay
- **Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka**: Fungal leaf disease causing yellow streaks/patches (Yellow Sigatoka) combined with black/dark necrotic lesions (Black Sigatoka/Black Leaf Streak). This precisely matches the extensive yellow discoloration **with** scattered dark/black spots on the same leaf tissue.

The hallmark combination of **yellow leaf discoloration** + **dark/black necrotic spots embedded within the yellowed tissue** on a banana leaf is diagnostic of Yellow and Black Sigatoka disease.
